quote: but I I don't want it on the roof.
stewart_read: This is a roof_or_home objection about mounting, not durability, and the rep answers a different question ('they won't damage your roof') instead of flipping it or probing what alternative the customer wants.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep could be strategically deferring to the specialist, but he never actually redirects cleanly — he keeps re-engaging with speculative answers instead.
coaching_implication: Should have asked immediately: 'when you say not on the roof, do you mean ground-mount, or no solar at all?' to size the real constraint before pitching anything.

quote: would that be an expense on my behalf to have to remove the panels and and reinstall them?
stewart_read: Rep answers a removal/reinstall cost question with a guess instead of using the escape hatch to the specialist immediately.
coaching_implication: Use the universal escape hatch verbatim earlier: 'that's exactly what the specialist is built to answer' — don't speculate on pricing.

quote: We do. But what does that have to do with what we're talking about?
stewart_read: The credit ask lands as a non-sequitur because the rep never framed why it matters, confusing an already-skeptical customer.
coaching_implication: Bridge qualifiers to purpose: 'since we don't have your utility bill yet, credit is the other way we can pre-qualify you' — ties the ask to logic instead of dropping it cold.

quote: So we have, like they're all black. They're a Tesla.
stewart_read: Unprompted panel-spec pitch (color, brand, durability) is closer-tier content the setter volunteers instead of redirecting.
coaching_implication: Redirect panel-appearance curiosity to the specialist call instead of describing product — this is exactly the anti-pattern the schema flags.

quote: I really don't want anything on the roof. I'll just say that up front.
stewart_read: Customer restates the core constraint post-booking and rep's response ('He'll [look at] this time') is noncommittal, not a real handshake on what happens next.
coaching_implication: This is the third touch of the same objection — should have been resolved with a clear yes/no on ground-mount options before ever setting a time.

quote: Okay. Then I don't because I just I know that he won't do anything but roof.
stewart_read: Rep effectively self-disqualifies the lead live on the call by admitting the specialist can't serve the customer's stated need, rather than checking if ground-mount or another product exists.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive read: this could plausibly be a true hard product gate (Ion only mounts on roofs) — but the rep never confirms this with a specialist or supervisor before killing the appointment himself.
coaching_implication: If roof-mount truly is Ion's only option, this should be confirmed and disclosed at 00:59, not discovered after four minutes of qualifying and a scheduled appointment.
